title: Microprompt Slate Adapter Protocol - Notes and Sketch
content:
Context / motivation:

This is a personal sketch for a small client-side adapter pattern I want to try: Microprompt Slate Adapter. The goal is to let product clients compose, cache, and prefetch small "slates" of prompt fragments (microprompts) that are stitched and optionally de-duplicated before being sent to Redwood's hosted API. Think: lightweight client-driven prompt assembly with explicit bounded invariants (size, TTL, intended partial reuse) and a small protocol for adapter -> runtime communication (hints for batching, prewarm, fallback).

Why? Common pain: when apps assemble dynamic prompts per user, we pay full token cost repeatedly for repeated fragments (system instructions, repeated context bits), and we lose opportunity to batch/merge across concurrent calls. Server-side caching and prefix caching helps, but clients are in the best position to declare what parts are stable and what can be reused across a session or across users (e.g., product description). The adapter should be able to:
- expose an ergonomic SDK API to register slates
- compactly describe slates to the runtime (hash + size + hint)
- request a prewarm / cache population that the server can use for KV-prefix caching
- be transparent about privacy (client indicates sensitive vs non-sensitive slates)

High level primitives (v0)
- Slate: an ordered list of microprompt fragments. Each fragment has an id, content (optional on-register), flags (sensitive, compressible), and a stability hint (session, user, global).
- SlateHandle: client-side opaque handle (slate_id + revision) used in subsequent generate calls.
- SlateManifest: short descriptor sent to server in place of full text when possible (hashes + length + hint).

Proposed minimal API (client SDK surface):

1) registerSlate(name, fragments[], opts) -> SlateHandle
   - name: optional alias for dev debugging
   - fragments: [{id: 'sys-1', text: 'You are a product assistant...', flags: ['system','compressible']} ...]
   - opts: {stability: 'session'|'user'|'global', ttl_sec: 3600, privacy: 'public'|'sensitive'}

2) updateFragment(slateHandle, fragmentId, newText) -> updatedHandle

3) generateWithSlate(slateHandle, callOverride) -> stream / response
   - callOverride is the normal Redwood generation args (temperature, model, extra prompt pieces).
   - Implementation: SDK will replace slate in the prompt body with a compact manifest when allowed, and attach the full slate text only if server requests it (or if privacy flags force full inclusion).

4) prewarmSlate(slateHandle, priority=normal) -> promise
   - hint to server that this slate will be used soon and should be included in prefix cache / prefetched KV state. Priority hints: low/normal/high.

5) retireSlate(slateHandle) -> void

Protocol shape (payloads to Redwood API)
- slate_manifest: {slate_id: <sha256>, fragments: [{fragment_id, hash, length}], total_tokens_estimate, stability, privacy, revision}  // compact
- slate_blob: {slate_id, revision, fragments: [{fragment_id, text, flags}], metadata} // only sent on register or if server asks

Server-side behaviors (rough):
- If request includes slate_manifest and server has matching cached prefix, it will expand server-side and proceed with reduced token accounting (billing note: client should still be aware of potential token differences).
- If server lacks the slate_blob, it returns a "missing_slate" code in the pre-flight / response headers with an inclusion policy (require-full-blob / request-on-miss / ignore). The SDK should automatically resend with slate_blob (respecting privacy).
- Prewarm requests may schedule background inclusion into KV caches and optionally trigger model hot-start warmups (GPU context preallocation).

ASCII flow diagram (client view):

Client app -> SDK.registerSlate()  (optional: send slate_blob to server)
Client app -> SDK.generateWithSlate(handle) -> HTTP POST to /v1/generate with body: {model, slate_manifest, prompt_tail}
Server: if cache hit -> expand + serve
        if miss -> respond 412 "missing_slate: slate_id" (or 202 async) -> SDK may resend with slate_blob or block based on privacy

Edge cases / heuristics:
- Fragment collisions: slug-based fragment ids are best-effort. Canonical identity is hash(content). Keep fragment ids for easier diffs.
- Partial reuse across models: manifest should include token-estimate per supported model family if possible; server may map to closest quantized variant.
- Privacy: if privacy==sensitive, do not send slate_blob to hosted servers unless explicitly allowed; instead, SDK can inline the fragments into prompt every call (no manifest). We need UX for admin override.
- Versioning: revision is monotonic integer. If client sends older revision than server knows, server should signal revision_mismatch and return current revision metadata.

Pseudocode example (SDK):

// register
let handle = sdk.registerSlate('signup-flow', [
  {id:'sys-a', text: 'You are an assistant that helps with signups.', flags:['system']},
  {id:'prod', text: 'Product: Redwood Inference - inference platform', flags:['informational']}
], {stability:'session', ttl_sec:7200});

// generate
let resp = sdk.generateWithSlate(handle, {model:'rwd-medium', max_tokens:512, prompt_tail:'User: how to integrate?'});

// on missing_slate -> SDK behavior
if (resp.status==412 && resp.body.code=='missing_slate') {
  if (handle.privacy!='sensitive') {
    sdk.sendSlateBlob(handle); // reissue generate
  } else {
    // degrade: inline full text locally and retry (billed normally)
  }
}

Telemetry and costs notes:
- Add explicit telemetry for: register frequency, manifest vs blob ratio, prewarm success rate, friction on private slates (users that frequently need inlining).
- Billing semantics: When manifest-only is used and server cache hits, token accounting should reflect server-side expansion to avoid double-billing; need product input.

Open questions / TODOs (iteration list):
- Do we want server to accept "partial manifests" (send subset of fragments) and expand missing ones by id? That enables delta sends but complicates miss logic.
- How to handle multi-tenant privacy when slates are global but include tenant text? Probably disallow global stability for tenant-specific slates.
- Define backoff rules for prewarm flood from many clients. Consider only allowing prewarm for high-priority slates or admin-whitelisted apps.
- SDK API ergonomics: should registerSlate be sync/async? I prefer async returning a handle that is usable immediately with manifest (optimistic).
- GC: local SDK should garbage collect slates not touched in TTL; server-side should evict based on TTL + prewarm signals.

Next practical experiment (MVP):
1) Implement minimal SDK as a layer on existing JS SDK: registerSlate(preferred: async) that returns manifest (sha256) and optional in-memory blob.
2) Server: accept slate_manifest in generate endpoint; if not present, return 412 with missing_slate list. Implement quick path to accept blob and cache prefix.
3) Run canary with internal product team (Aisha P) on a low-volume feature to measure manifest-hit ratio.

Notes to self: keep the first iteration small. Avoid trying to do complex cross-model token estimates; do a single-model-backed MVP. Add clear admin controls for privacy opt-in. Link this to the ongoing prefix-caching work (ENG-4213).

Slack threads / references: slack #sdk-libs "microprompt slate" 2024-11-12 (brain dump), PR draft https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/398

End of sketch.
